Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

My 5 mu is small, so I cannot afford a bad harvest. My wife's brother works in Handan and sends some money, and I do some construction work in winter, but the grain still matters — it feeds us and the pigs.

**Winter wheat (planted last October, will harvest this June):**
I already planted in October like always. I used Jimai 22 — improved variety, my neighbor Old Wang has been getting 500 kg/mu with it for three years, so I stayed with it. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15, 40 kg) per mu as base fertilizer before planting, then I will topdress urea at jointing in early March — about 15 kg/mu. That gives me around 14 kg nitrogen total, plus the 6 from compound. Actually let me count again: 40 kg of 15-15-15 gives 6 kg N, 6 P, 6 K per mu. Then 15 kg urea (46% N) gives about 7 more kg N. So roughly 13 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. That is a bit low for my area. I will add another 10 kg urea at booting because last year my wheat looked yellow. So around 18 kg N total.

Wait — I need to be honest. People around here usually use more. I will do 40 kg compound at base, then 20 kg urea at jointing, then maybe 10 more if it looks pale. Better to spend the extra 30 yuan than lose 50 kg of grain.

Irrigation: winter water in December (already done), then jointing water in March, then grain-filling water in May. Three times from my well. Pesticide: one spray for aphids and powdery mildew in April, one for wheat midge if I see them. Two sprays usually enough.

Rotary tillage — everyone uses the rotary machine here, 40 yuan per mu for the service.

**Summer maize (will plant after wheat harvest in mid-June):**
I will plant Zhengdan 958 again. Straight into the wheat stubble, no-till with the seeder — saves time and money, and the moisture stays in the ground. 

For fertilizer, I put one bag of compound (50 kg of 15-15-15) as starter with the seed, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage (about 6 leaves) — 25 kg/mu urea. That gives me about 19 kg N, 7.5 P, 7.5 K per mu. Maize is a heavy feeder but my field has good residue from wheat straw returned, so this should work.

Irrigation: maize here usually gets one emergence water and one at tasseling if rain is short. Two times. Pesticide: one for armyworm/corn borer, maybe one for aphid. Two times.

Yield target: wheat 500 kg/mu, maize 550 kg/mu. That is what my neighbors get in a normal year.
